_comment:
Closes the hole in the witness check. A witness's death used to be an annotation on the charter's own witness list, so a forger who simply declined to write obiit defeated the whole test by omission. Deaths live out here now, in a book he never touched.

NOTE what this is NOT. It is not a necrology of the Empire, because a complete one would be an oracle and an oracle ends the game. It is one partial extract in its own hand, written up only so far, followed by three houses that return nothing at all. Absence from this roll is NEVER evidence of life.

Matching is on person_id and never on the name. Two men may be called Hugo Wend, and one of them may be in nobody's roll at all.

book.title: The Kalendar of the Dead
book.subtitle: obits returned to this Chancery, and by whom
book._cover_note: THE MEMORANDUM SAYS 'the green book in the rack is the Kalendar', and until now that sentence was false. #2a2f2a is (42,47,42) — green by five parts in 255, which is neutral. The room's only light is a candle, so every surface is multiplied by roughly (1.0, 0.6, 0.3) and the cover rendered RED-dominant at a measured mean of (18.3, 12.6, 11.3). There was no green book in the rack; it was distinguishable from the Register only as the less maroon one. Green now leads by enough to survive the warm multiply, at the same value as the Almanac's olive and the Matrices' brown so it does not read as a different class of object.
book.front_matter:
This Chancery keeps no roll of its own dead and never has. What it keeps here is one extract returned by the Margrave's chapel at Thurnstadt, copied in the order that book was written, with its hand named at the head.

Read the head before you read the names. The chapel says whose dead it keeps, how it counts an emperor's years, and how far its writing has reached.
book.front_matter_two: Read the covering line also. It says whose dead that house undertook to keep, and no more than that. A man who is not in a roll is not thereby living; he may only be a man that roll was never keeping.
book.marginalia: One house answers and three do not. In eleven years at this desk I have never once been able to write down that a man was living — only that nobody has sent word he was dead. — R.V.

rolls.covers: the Margrave's household and the ministeriales
rolls.note: A house that breaks a die before witnesses on the day its holder dies learns very quickly to write the day down. These years are the Chancery's own, counted from the accession, and this chapel will stand behind every one of them.
rolls.marginalia: This roll and the Book of Matrices put Dietrich in the same year, which is the only time two sources in this office have ever agreed without being made to. — R.V.

entries.name: Eckhard von Melle
entries.title: marshal of Thurn
entries.note: Marshal four-and-twenty years. Died at Marchfeld in the same season as the Emperor, and was carried home.

entries.name: Dietrich
entries.title: Margrave of Thurn
entries.note: His die was defaced in this chapel the same day, before nine witnesses, as the March requires.

entries.name: Herbord Gantz
entries.title: castellan of Thurnstadt
entries.note: Held the castle eleven years. Buried beneath this chapel, on the north side, with his wife.

entries.name: Folkwin Tanne
entries.title: forester of the Vech
entries.note: Taken by the water at the alder bank. Six weeks in the finding of him.

silent.reason: Ostmark is partible: Berthold's four sons keep four foundations and four kalendars between them, and no one of them will answer for the dead of a Duchy that is already in quarters.
The Count keeps a roll and will not send it — R.V. wrote to Ulrich four times and had one reply, which said that the dead of Hallenstein are Hallenstein's affair.
The Wends keep no writing of any kind, and the few extracts a clerk once made for us burnt with the archive at Lenz in '18.
